name: Perpetual Hesitation

detectability.signature: Vacuum energy fluctuations visible as instrument static with structure; virtual particle pair production at macroscopic scales registers as shimmering mass-that-isn't

proximity: Sensors display structured static that almost resolves into patterns
Small objects aboard flicker between positions millimeters apart
contact: Solid matter becomes probabilistic; hull sections exist in superposed states until observed
Instruments report each reading simultaneously true and false
prolonged_exposure: Crew members begin to decohere from a single history, sharing memories of mutually exclusive events
Ship systems fail as components refuse, statistically, to remain assembled

phenomena: Quantum uncertainty manifesting at macro scale: coins landing both ways, dials holding several values
Matter spontaneously changing state within the boundary, ice boiling and vapor freezing
Exotic particles detectable on sensors that decay before their detection is complete
Unusual gravitational readings despite negligible aggregate mass
hazards: Genetic mutation from stochastic molecular reordering during exposure
Equipment malfunction from timeline and state interference
Crew disappearance, recorded once, when a technician decohered fully during repair work
opportunities: Test exotic theories of quantum gravity under conditions impossible to engineer
Unique material synthesis: matter conditioned here retains useful probabilistic properties
Data valuable to scientific institutions, sold at premiums that fund three permanent stations
known_incidents: Technician Amal Voss vanished during a hull repair inside the foam in 2396; her tools returned, her logbook's final entry was written in two handwritings
The materials consortium Ferrolattice pays hazard wages considered generous even by salvage standards for foam-conditioned alloys
description: Perpetual Hesitation is invisible, nine thousand kilometers of vacuum where the universe forgot to make up its mind. Instruments detect it as static with structure, readings that shimmer on the edge of meaning, and mass readings that add up differently every time they are summed. Physicists believe it is a region where primordial quantum foam never settled into smooth spacetime.

The boundary expands irregularly, sometimes gaining a hundred kilometers in a day, sometimes surrendering them back. Inside, probability misbehaves politely at first: dials hold two values, small objects sit in two places. Deeper in, matter itself grows undecided, and hull plating has been observed to be unbreached and holed at once until someone looked properly.

It has existed since the beginning, older than any star, and was only found thirteen years ago when a courier's chronometer began reporting yesterday. The Voss incident remains its only confirmed casualty and its most studied document, particularly an entry written in two handwritings at once. Three research stations orbit permanently, funded by institutions that consider uncertainty a resource.

Ferrolattice harvests foam-conditioned alloys whose odd statistical properties command extraordinary prices, and their crews wear the field's hazard pay like a uniform. The foam continues its slow argument with definition, expanding and retreating without malice or pattern. Travelers are advised to cross quickly, look at nothing twice, and trust whichever version of their instruments apologizes first.
